chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from Yasin al-Darir, from Hariz, from al-Fadl, who said:

I performed Hajj with my family in a year when sacrificial animals were scarce, so I went and bought two sheep at a high price. When I threw down their two hides, I regretted it with deep regret because of the leanness I saw in them. So I went to him (the Imam) and informed him of that, and he said, 'If there is any fat on their kidneys, it is sufficient (valid).'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a lean animal to be valid for sacrifice in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* highlights the practical flexibility in fiqh regarding the physical condition of sacrificial animals, prioritizing the presence of essential fat (kullah) over general robustness. It reflects the Shia scholarly approach of avoiding undue hardship (la haraj) when economic constraints, such as scarcity and high prices, necessitate purchasing leaner animals. The ruling underscores that the validity of the udhiyah is not contingent upon ideal aesthetic qualities but rather on the specific anatomical marker of fat on the kidneys.
